summary: This benchmark article reports an ablation study evaluating the effect of equalizing initial saved-word states across controllers during periodic 3D boundary jumps on a 192³ lattice. By controlling for diverged history via a shared saved-word bank, the authors demonstrate that the sparse sensing retention advantage (1.37 percentage points) remains robust and statistically indistinguishable from the separate-bank gain (1.47 percentage points). The methodology is sound, well-isolated, and reproducible, though heavily dependent on the context of the author's previous staggered-jump simulation framework.
strengths: Rigorous experimental ablation isolating saved-state history from runtime boundary-tracking performance.
Careful statistical treatment including bootstrap resampling of complete worlds and pre-registered tolerance boundaries.
Comprehensive environmental documentation including hardware specifications, library versions, memory footprints, and execution runtimes.
weaknesses: High contextual coupling with preceding work, making the benchmark somewhat opaque without reading prior study specifications.
Evaluation is limited to a single synthetic fault family, frozen checkpoint weights, and eight simulated worlds, constraining generalizability.
suggestions: Include a brief diagram or explicit explanation of the lattice read rule and write-pulse fault dynamics within the main text for self-containment.
Expand testing across multiple checkpoint weights or varying boundary jump magnitudes to evaluate sensitivity beyond the single fault family.

claims.text: The periodic 192³ lattice stores a working 32-bit word and a saved 32-bit word at each cell, representing 7.08 million cells.
With each controller starting from the same 7.08-million-cell saved-word bank at every jump, sparse sensing improved first-round retention over stale calibration by 1.37 percentage points.
claims.source: Internal arithmetic consistency: Table values show sparse sensing (74.23%) minus stale calibration (72.86%) = 1.37%.

claims.text: The original comparison, in which each controller kept its own saved words, gained 1.47 points.
